title: Common finite coefficient field for a pair of lattice generators
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E_1,E_2\subset\Qlb$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $a_i:Z_i\hookrightarrow W_i$ be locally closed immersions, with $W_1=X,W_2=Y$. Let $L_i$ be lisse finite free $\cO_{E_i,Z_i}$-modules, meaning that on a pro-etale covering they are finite rank free modules over that pulled-back coefficient ring. Put $G_i=\Qlb_{W_i}\otimes^L_{\cO_{E_i,W_i}}a_{i!}L_i$, where $a_{i!}$ is exact locally closed extension by zero. Then there is a finite subextension $F\subset\Qlb$ containing both $E_i$. For $L_{i,F}=\cO_{F,Z_i}\otimes_{\cO_{E_i,Z_i}}L_i$, each $L_{i,F}$ is lisse finite free and $K_{i,F}=a_{i!}L_{i,F}$ lies in $\Dbc(W_i,\cO_F)$. Scalar transitivity and scalar/extension-by-zero comparison give canonical isomorphisms $\Qlb_{W_i}\otimes^L_{\cO_{F,W_i}}K_{i,F}\cong G_i$.

source.place: paragraph (3), pairs of Qlbar generators before devissage; former step 8

proof.text: Take $F=E_1E_2\subseteq\Qlb$. Clause (1) of [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions], applied to this two-element family, says that $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite and contains both $E_i$. Thus this is one actual finite subfield for the two generators, independent of their strata or their local ranks.

source.place: paragraph (3), pairs of Qlbar generators before devissage; former step 8; common finite field argument, step 1

proof.text: Use the valuation inherited from the fixed valued field $\Qlb$. By the valuation-ring description in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $\cO_{E_i}=E_i\cap\cO_F$, so the inclusions restrict to continuous ring maps $\cO_{E_i}\to\cO_F$. They send a continuous function to the same function with the larger codomain, hence induce maps of the continuous-function condensed rings. Their composites with $\cO_F\to\Qlb$ are the original inclusions, already on each section. Apply the functorial coefficient change of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] on $Z_i$ and $W_i$ to obtain the corresponding ring-sheaf towers. All these are the coefficient maps used below.

source.place: paragraph (3), pairs of Qlbar generators before devissage; former step 8; common finite field argument, step 2

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] on $(Z_i)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ with $R=\cO_{E_i,Z_i}$, $B=\cO_{F,Z_i}$ and $M=L_i$. The hypothesis is exactly the assumed pro-etale local finite freeness: a cover of $Z_i$ restricts to a trivializing cover over every site object. It gives that $L_{i,F}=B\otimes_R L_i$ is lisse finite free with the same local ranks, and the canonical identification $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L_i[0]\cong L_{i,F}[0]$. In particular this calculation requires no assertion that the whole coefficient-change functor is exact and no uniform bound on local ranks.

source.place: paragraph (3), pairs of Qlbar generators before devissage; former step 8; common finite field argument, step 3

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [det-lem-integral-models-generators] with coefficient field $F$, ambient standing scheme $W_i$, locally closed immersion $a_i$, and lisse finite free lattice $L_{i,F}$ from step 3. That clause writes $a_{i!}$ as closed direct image after open extension by zero, $a_{i!}=c_*u_!$ for a factorization $a_i=c\circ u$ with $u$ open and $c$ closed; [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] ($W_i$ is Noetherian, being of finite type over $k$) gives the normalized identification of this functor with the exact locally closed extension by zero of the statement, $a_{i!}\cong c_*u_!$. Since $\Dbc(W_i,\cO_F)$ is closed under isomorphism, it gives $K_{i,F}=a_{i!}L_{i,F}\in\Dbc(W_i,\cO_F)$. These are precisely the hypotheses of that clause; no integral-model existence assertion is needed.

source.place: paragraph (3), pairs of Qlbar generators before devissage; former step 8; common finite field argument, step 4

proof.text:
Put $T^V_{A,B}=B_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_V}-$ for coefficient rings in the tower $A=\cO_{E_i}\to B=\cO_F\to C=\Qlb$. Clause (2) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback], applied to $a_i$ and $L_i[0]$, and the degree-zero comparison of step 3 give $T^{W_i}_{A,B}(a_{i!}L_i)\cong a_{i!}(T^{Z_i}_{A,B}L_i)\cong a_{i!}L_{i,F}=K_{i,F}$. Apply $T^{W_i}_{B,C}$ to the inverse of this isomorphism, then clause (3) of the same cited node. The resulting canonical composite is
$$\Qlb_{W_i}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\cO_{F,W_i}}K_{i,F}\ \cong\ T^{W_i}_{B,C}T^{W_i}_{A,B}(a_{i!}L_i)\ \cong\ T^{W_i}_{A,C}(a_{i!}L_i)=G_i.$$
The composite coefficient map is the original inclusion by step 2. The scalar/immersion and tower comparisons in the cited statement are natural, so this is the claimed canonical comparison for each $i$.
